segments.narration: Two children with bright green skin emerged from a dense forest. In 12th-century England, villagers in Woolpit found a boy and girl who spoke no known language and wore strange, unknown clothing.

They wept in terror and refused all local food, nearly starving until they stumbled upon raw green beans. As they slowly adjusted to normal meals, the mysterious green hue on their skin began to fade away.

segments.narration: Once the girl learned English, she claimed they came from a sunless subterranean realm called St. Martin's Land. Was this a genuine fairy tale, or something far more human?
Historians finally solved the mystery. In 1173, royal persecution forced Flemish immigrants to flee into dark underground flint mines near Fornham St. Martin, where many died.

Severe iron deficiency from tunnel starvation causes chlorosis—a medical condition that literally tints human skin green. The mysterious green children were simply orphaned refugees who survived in the dark.
